To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the model independent perturbation theory approach to the description of QCD cascades in the leading logarithmic approximation is not applicable for the description of the particle spectra produced in e+e− annhilation.
the modified LL approximation is a good tool for the analysis of the particle spectra and that the local parton–hadron duality concept works well for inclusive energy spectra in QCD parton jets.

The leading-logarithmic approximation is not sufficient to describe the inclusive spectra of hadrons in the region of large transverse momenta, where the logarithmically enhanced contributions from higher orders in the perturbation theory are expected to dominate.

The main takeaway from our work is that
the modified leading logarithm approximation is a viable alternative for description of Qcd jet physics.
the model independent perturbation theory can be used to describe the inclusive spectra of particles produced in jets with a precision of about 10% in the whole kinematic range of the experiments.
